key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates thermal degradation, with losses spreading into the perovskite absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers evaluate whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent excitation photoluminescence to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decay signatures with diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination from fullerene deposition after PEABF4 treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support the interface-to-bulk interpretation.
watch_item: Depth attribution relies on model-supported interpretation, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
